source.title: Advisory Actions of the General Service Conference of Alcoholics Anonymous 1951–2026
source.note: Summaries are written for this app in plain words; the original wording is in the PDF (open the page link).

sections.name: Other Countries and World Service Meetings

actions.text: Agreed that nonalcoholic trustees should keep serving on the Alcoholic Foundation’s board.
Required Conference approval for future A.A. textbook literature, clarifying this would neither stop nor censor material put out locally or by outside sources.
Recommended a fixed term of office for the board’s alcoholic trustees.
Limited attendance at the 1952 Conference sessions to Conference members: delegates, Foundation trustees, and accredited GSO and Grapevine staff.

due.what: Conference sessions open only to Conference members

actions.text: Sent back without a decision: the question of A.A. auxiliaries or family groups went to local groups for discussion, to be taken up at the 1952 Conference.

due.what: Conference to consider auxiliaries/family groups after local discussion

actions.text: Found the temporary charter in the Third Legacy pamphlet workable for three more years and approved the general principles guiding assemblies.

due.what: end of the three-year period the temporary charter was judged suitable for

actions.text: The Agenda Committee would consult every Conference committee, the trustees, and GSO before proposing topics for the 1953 Conference.

due.what: topics for the 1953 Conference proposed after consulting committees, trustees and GSO

actions.text: Praised the staff-led panels with delegates’ remarks and asked that they be kept in the 1954 program.

due.what: repeat the staff-led panels in the program

actions.text: When a controversial issue stalls on the floor, the chair should draw second-year delegates by lot to meet separately and return with a recommendation.

due.what: closed-session agenda suggestions due 90 days before the Conference

actions.text: Directed that the first business session open with readings of the Chapter V preamble from the Big Book, the Twelve Steps, and the Twelve Traditions.
Each day’s opening session to begin with a prayer as delegates suggest; all other sessions to start with a short silence.
The Conference’s final session to close with the Lord’s Prayer.
Area Delegates Only sessions to be chaired by a second-year delegate, with a first-year vice-chair who becomes chair the following year.
Asked GSO to keep holding briefing sessions for new delegates before the Conference begins.
Judged a full afternoon too long for the Grapevine; its report should be shortened to key facts on finances, circulation, and trends.
Asked GSO to keep briefing new delegates ahead of Conference deliberations.
Gave GSO staff reports more time for human-interest stories, scheduling them first and back to back, about ten minutes each.
Kept the selection of Conference committees as the second item of business on opening morning.
Limited the General Service Board’s report and each of its committees’ reports to five minutes, scheduled with other business at the second Conference session (that afternoon) or later.
Continued GSO’s briefing session for new delegates before the Conference opens.
Limited delegates’ remarks from the floor to three minutes.
Display the Puerto Rican flag alongside the U.S. and Canadian flags at future Conferences.
Continued an agenda modeled on the 1960 Conference’s.
Area highlights to be split evenly between first-year and second-year delegates.
Set clock limits for Conference participation: panel chairs 10 minutes, panel speakers and reports 5, area highlights 3, floor comments 2.
Moved the Area-Delegates-Only meeting earlier in the week, to Thursday evening.
Area highlights should keep addressing subjects tied to the 1963 Conference theme.

due.what: area highlights to address the 1963 Conference theme

actions.text: Agenda subjects should reach the Agenda Committee year-round, and the July and October Policy Committee meetings should also review discussion subjects.
Any important agenda subject arising after the October tentative agenda, plus any item it would replace, should go to the Agenda Committee before the board decides.
The Agenda Committee should propose specific subjects before the agenda is finalized.
Asked GSO to consider over the year a fitting expression of gratitude to Bill W. and Lois W., to be presented at the 1964 Conference.

due.what: present an expression of gratitude to Bill W. and Lois W.

actions.text: Agenda items left off the current agenda should pass to the next year’s committee.
Area highlights to continue centering on one theme.

actions.text: Scheduled the Area Delegate Only meeting for the 1965 Conference’s third evening.

due.what: Area Delegate Only meeting on the third evening

actions.text: Explain Conference committees’ duties fully before members are chosen for them at future Conferences.

actions.text: Inform delegates of major issues ahead of time so they can read materials and discuss them before voting.

actions.text: Given the heavy agenda, mark some lower-priority items as optional so they can be dropped if time runs short.

actions.text: Reaffirmed the need at every level to identify interested members and build understanding of professional relations within the Traditions and primary purpose.
No special literature for law-enforcement officials is needed; existing A.A. material serves that purpose.
The Grapevine’s gray pages already cover alcoholism-field news adequately, so no new publication is needed.
Assembly and committee discussions, perhaps a “Live and Let Live” workshop, could clarify the role of members who wear “two hats.”
Reaffirmed that members working in the alcoholism field may be elected to service at any level; choices should rest on A.A. activity, not employment.
Where possible, area members should help alcoholism counselors start A.A. meetings in treatment centers rather than leave it to the counselors.
Noted that professionals reach A.A. through intergroup offices, answering services and personal contact, and in some places it is common knowledge.
Forming area C.P.C. committees would boost understanding and cooperation within each area.
Renamed the “Conference Committee on Professional Relations” as the “Conference Committee on Cooperation with the Professional Community,” to be written out in full, not abbreviated.
Allowed showing “Bill’s Own Story” during A.A. orientations at rehab facilities, provided an A.A. member is in charge of it.
Noted a continuing shortage of sponsorship in some areas, even though most members can tell Twelfth Step work, sponsorship and referral apart.
With “two-hatters,” attitudes rather than titles are the issue; renaming could be considered if it would actually change attitudes.
Continue cooperating with professionals because it helps carry the message, following Bill W.’s advice to stay friendly with our friends.
Sharing more results of professional–A.A. cooperation could improve understanding of professionals’ work in alcoholism.
All members, including those working professionally in the field, should study the Traditions more, improving relations with professionals and each other.
Dropped the term “two hatter” from official literature in favor of “A.A. member employed in the field of alcoholism” or similar.
Ended discussion of John O.’s letter about a Phoenix hospital and gave a nonalcoholic (Class A) trustee a unanimous vote of confidence.
Make more use of the existing service structure to carry out the committee’s recommendations.
Offered members seeking alcoholism-field work tips: use existing literature, get training, have three to five years’ sobriety, keep a sponsor outside the field, know the Steps and Traditions.
To help sponsor newcomers from treatment and court programs: improve contact with referral sources, meet newcomers where they are, and set up sponsorship programs for treatment-center referrals.
G.S.O. to write a paper for court and agency referrals and their staff explaining A.A.’s stance on signing forms and the kinds of meetings available.
Encouraged members to join C.P.C. committees and cooperate with P.I. and institutions committees, e.g., sponsor your doctor, clergy and employer, reach academia, hold workshops.
In a spirit of cooperation, answer every call for information about A.A., whether from an alcoholic or from a professional calling for a client.
Reaffirmed the 1976 C.P.C. Committee’s advice to meet newcomers where they are, along with its entire 1976 report.
A joint Conference–trustee meeting of the P.I., C.P.C. and Institutions committees was impractical; the board should consider a joint trustees’ meeting before the 1978 Conference to clarify roles.

Members forming a group in a treatment facility should explain autonomy and A.A.’s limits, learn facility rules, inform attending members, practice self-support, and not let employed members run it.

Through C.P.C. committees, members should tell treatment facilities and court programs which meetings, including beginners meetings, are available, respect group autonomy, and offer sponsorship to newcomers.
Reaffirmed the 1976 recommendation encouraging members to join C.P.C. committees, cooperate with P.I. and institutions committees, and sponsor doctors, clergy and employers.

Renew efforts to teach members working in alcoholism about the Traditions and the “Guidelines for A.A. Members Employed in the Alcoholism Field.”
Continue C.P.C. work; with many newcomers arriving, groups should stress primary purpose by greeting newcomers, embracing sponsorship and taking periodic group inventories.
